titles.li: Shelter the pilgrims and their relic

texts.li: [fellowship] A group of {COUNT} pilgrims of {FACTION}, led by {GIVER}, is walking from shrine to shrine with a relic of their faith. They ask to rest at the colony for a few days.
[!fellowship] A group of {COUNT} pilgrims of {FACTION}, led by {GIVER}, is on its way to a holy place with a relic of their faith. They ask to rest at the colony for a few days.

li.label: Let them rest here
li.outcome: The pilgrims are on their way.

li.label: Decline
li.outcome: The pilgrims will rest somewhere else.

lines.li: [stolen] The relic is gone, someone has taken it.
[judge] You caught the thief, so you should decide what happens now.
[handed] We will take this one home to answer to our elders.
[punished] Then the thief is in your hands.
[letgo] You are kinder than we would have been.
[escaped] Our relic was taken while we slept under your roof.

terms.li: If the colony agrees, the pilgrims come within a day and stay about {DAYS}. Each of them needs a bed or sleeping spot under a roof, and meals from the colony's stores, {ITEM} in all. If the stores have nothing for them, they eat what they brought.\n\n{GIVER} carries the relic and will set it down where the pilgrims sleep. If they are well looked after, {FACTION} will be grateful.

accepted.li: {COUNT} pilgrims of {FACTION} are on their way to the colony with their relic.

notes.li: [came] The pilgrims of {FACTION} are arriving. {GIVER} will set their relic down where they sleep.
[stranger] A traveller, {RIVAL}, has asked the pilgrims of {FACTION} for a place by their fire for the night.
[stolen,own] In the night {RIVAL}, one of the pilgrims, took their relic and is running for the edge of the map with it. Stop {RIVAL} before {RIVAL} gets away.
[stolen,stranger] In the night {RIVAL}, the traveller who shared the pilgrims' fire, took their relic and is running for the edge of the map with it. Stop {RIVAL} before {RIVAL} gets away.
[caught] {RIVAL} has been caught, and the relic is back. The pilgrims ask the colony to decide what happens to {RIVAL}.
[back] The pilgrims' relic is back, and {GIVER} will take it again.

ends.li: [handed] The pilgrims of {FACTION} have gone on with their relic, and they took {RIVAL} with them to answer to their own people.
[punished] The pilgrims of {FACTION} have gone on with their relic. {RIVAL} is the colony's prisoner.
[letgo] The pilgrims of {FACTION} have gone on with their relic. The colony let {RIVAL} go.
[killed] {RIVAL} died with the relic, and the pilgrims of {FACTION} have gone on with it.
[dropped] {RIVAL} got away without the relic, and the pilgrims of {FACTION} have gone on with it.
[escaped] {RIVAL} got away with the relic. The pilgrims of {FACTION} blame the colony for it, and have gone on without it.
[harmed] The pilgrims of {FACTION} or their relic came to harm in the colony's care. They will not forget it.

texts.li: [own] {RIVAL}, one of the pilgrims, took their relic in the night and was caught. The pilgrims ask the colony to decide what happens to {RIVAL}.\n\nThe colony can hand {RIVAL} over to the pilgrims, who will take {RIVAL} home to answer to their own people. It can keep {RIVAL} as the colony's prisoner. Or it can let {RIVAL} go.

[stranger] {RIVAL}, a traveller who shared the pilgrims' fire, took their relic in the night and was caught. The pilgrims ask the colony to decide what happens to {RIVAL}.\n\nThe colony can hand {RIVAL} over to the pilgrims, who will take {RIVAL} with them. It can keep {RIVAL} as the colony's prisoner. Or it can let {RIVAL} go.

titles.li: [camp] Get the relic back from the thief's camp

texts.li: [camp] A day or two ago {RIVAL} got away from the colony with the pilgrims' relic, and {FACTION} blame the colony for it. Their scouts have found {RIVAL}'s camp close to the colony, and {GIVER} asks the colony to get the relic back.

[!camp] A day or two ago {RIVAL} got away from the colony with the pilgrims' relic, and {FACTION} blame the colony for it. The pilgrims will go after {RIVAL} themselves, and {GIVER} asks the colony for food for the road.

li.label: Decline
li.outcome: The pilgrims of {FACTION} are on their own now.

terms.li: [camp] If the colony agrees, {RIVAL}'s camp, a camp of {OTHERPEOPLE} within three tiles of the colony, is marked on the world map for {DAYS}. The colony's people can go there as a caravan. {RIVAL} and the relic are inside, with fighters of {OTHERPEOPLE}. Bring the relic home to the colony before the camp moves on.\n\nIf the relic comes home, the pilgrims will come for it. If not, it is lost to them.

[!camp] If the colony agrees, it puts {ITEM} in its stockpiles within a day and a half, and the pilgrims' people come for it. With the food, the pilgrims are more likely to find {RIVAL}. They send word within a few days.\n\nIf they find the relic, they will come back to the colony. If not, it is lost to them.

accepted.li: [camp] {RIVAL}'s camp is marked on the world map. Bring the relic home within {DAYS}.
[!camp] The colony will put {ITEM} in its stockpiles for the pilgrims of {FACTION}.

notes.li: [setout] The pilgrims of {FACTION} have the colony's food and have set out after {RIVAL}.
[setoutshort] The pilgrims of {FACTION} have set out after {RIVAL} without the colony's food.

ends.li: [recovered,camp] The pilgrims' relic is back at the colony. {GIVER} of {FACTION} will come for it.
[recovered,!camp] The pilgrims of {FACTION} found {RIVAL} and took their relic back. They are grateful for the colony's help.
[notfound] The pilgrims' relic was not found, and {FACTION} have given it up for lost.

titles.li: Keep the relic at the colony's shrine

texts.li: [!recovered] When the pilgrims' relic was taken at the colony, the colony got it back. {GIVER} of {FACTION} now asks to leave it at the colony's shrine for a year, so that pilgrims can come to see it there.

[recovered] When the pilgrims' relic was stolen, the colony helped them get it back. {GIVER} of {FACTION} now asks to leave it at the colony's shrine for a year, so that pilgrims can come to see it there.

li.label: Decline
li.outcome: The pilgrims will take the relic home.

lines.li: [laid] It will be safe here with you for the year.

terms.li: [!noshrine] If the colony agrees, {GIVER} comes within a day and sets the relic down beside the colony's shrine. It stays there for a year. Once a season pilgrims of {FACTION} come to see it and leave an offering, and at the end of the year {GIVER} comes and takes it home.\n\nThe relic must stay at the colony while it is there. If it is lost, {FACTION} will hold it against the colony.

[noshrine] The colony has no shrine yet: an altar, a shrine, a ritual spot or a work of art. If the colony agrees, it has {DAYS} to put one up, and then {GIVER} comes and sets the relic down beside it. It stays there for a year. Once a season pilgrims of {FACTION} come to see it and leave an offering, and at the end of the year {GIVER} comes and takes it home.\n\nIf there is no shrine by then, {GIVER} takes the relic home. If the relic is lost while it is at the colony, {FACTION} will hold it against the colony.

accepted.li: {GIVER} of {FACTION} is bringing the relic to the colony's shrine.

notes.li: [came] {GIVER} of {FACTION} has come with the relic.

ends.li: [kept] {GIVER} of {FACTION} has set the relic down beside the {ITEM}. It will stay at the colony for a year, and pilgrims will come to see it.
[noshrine] The colony had no shrine for the relic, so {GIVER} has taken it home.
